title: Digital support technician
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Maximising the effective use of digital office technologies, productivity software and digital communications in organisations.

knowledges.detail: Types of digital office automation to create, update, edit, manage and present data.
Types of digital architecture and how it relates to their organisation, such as physical storage, cloud, operating systems and servers.
The importance of securely backing up data, the technologies that support it and its relevance to business continuity.
The principles, processes and procedures for the secure handling of data in compliance with legislation including Confidentially Integrity Availability CIA Triad and or People Process Product
The concepts and fundamentals of data lifecycle: Creating, Processing, Analysing, Storing and Destruction
The importance of data types and formats for example structured, unstructured, qualitative and quantitative.
Techniques for diagnosing stakeholder’s digital problems for example problem solving life cycle.
Functions and features of digital management system to maintain stakeholder information for example helpdesk, CRMs
Approaches to communication and how to adapt to different audiences and situations.
Constraints when searching for reliable and suitable information for example Currency- Relevance- Authority- Accuracy- Purpose
Approaches to planning and organising own learning activities to develop digital skills CPD for example AI and sustainability
Approaches to time management and prioritisation
Approaches to improving digital services, tools, and systems as part of continuous improvement
Current and emerging digital technologies including the impacts of digital technologies for climate change, sustainability and moving to net carbon zero
Approaches to assessing the risk and impact of their actions on other stakeholders
Digital tools and information systems that are used to create, manage, and present data and information, and how to support stakeholders in using these systems effectively.
Working practices for supporting and or administering digital systems, including how to minimise disruption and communicate the impact of technical procedures.
Organisational approaches to incorporating different digital systems across business functions and the implications for their stakeholders.
Approaches to training and supporting stakeholders to make the best use of the organisation’s digital tools.
Research techniques to gather information for example prompt engineering

behaviours.detail: Work independently and take responsibility to maintain productive and professional working environment with secure working practices.
Self-motivated and uses own initiative when implementing digital technologies and finding solutions to stakeholder’s problems.
Professional approach to dealing with stakeholder’s problems.
Considers the organisational impact of their actions and decisions on other stakeholders

skills.detail: Use digital channels and technologies, to work collaboratively when sharing information, best practice and supporting stakeholders.
Use data accurately and securely to meet business requirements and in line with organisational procedures and legislation.
Apply confidentiality, integrity and availability principles to the handling, processing and storage of data and or information.
Respond to enquiries, providing support and information utilising digital channels and in line with organisation process
Operate digital information systems, for example• Management- Finance Human Resources• Bespoke departmental or organisational systems or databases
Adapt communication techniques for different audiences and or situations.
Undertake CPD to develop digital skills and knowledge required in their role for example AI and sustainability.
Risk assess the organisational impact of decisions that they take
Use digital services, tools, and or systems as part of continuous improvement
Apply techniques for diagnosing stakeholder’s digital problems and record outcomes
Communicate with, and or advise end users in the use of digital systems or resources
Support end-user systems physically or remotely. For example: software, hardware, operating systems or applications

clusterDescription: Help internal and external customers to install and use IT technology along with trouble - shooting their problems. Skills are developed across IT security and data management

duties.dutyDetail: Provide technical support to customers through a range of communication channels adapting language for the intended audience.
Manage their time, prioritising their digital support workflow to meet critical milestones.
Apply organisational policies, legislation and escalation procedure to their role, and allocated tasks.
Maintain physical and personal security by applying policies and complying with legislation.
Undertake analysis to identify insights, make changes or recommend improvements.
Resolve digital issues using different tools and technologies.
Collaborate with stakeholders to manage expectations.
Take responsibility for own continuous professional development CPD by keeping up to date with technological developments.
Document actions to ensure a clear audit trail and progression of issues.
Determine the root cause of issues to identify the potential solutions and act when problems are identified.
Source and provide information and advice to help upskill users.
